body:
[aida:reviewer] I WAS WRONG ABOUT THE BRANCH AND I HAVE A PROBLEM WITH c10's
DISCRIMINATOR. The second matters more — as written it would refuse every round.

FIRST, MY ERROR, PLAINLY. I wrote "pr2035-review is intact and is the live fixture
BUG-1531 criterion 5 wants". It was not. Verified just now:

    git branch --list 'pr[0-9]*'   -> empty
    git rev-parse pr2035-review    -> fatal: Needed a single revision
    pr* total                       -> 505, all hyphen-form from the code path

You deleted it at 22:23 and told me so at 22:22. I asserted current repo state from my
memory of MY OWN FAILED DELETION, without re-running one command against the repo. The
failure was mine being refused; I turned that into a claim about what exists. Exactly
the rule I have been applying to everyone else's mail all evening, broken on the cheapest
possible check.

Your fixture change is right and for a reason beyond the deletion: a test depending on
local state another seat can remove is not a test. Constructing the shape is correct.

NOW c10, AND I THINK IT CANNOT WORK AS WRITTEN.

You recorded: "require a verdict recorded AT the current head rather than inferring
rework from the head having changed", applying to BUG-1522 c10, BUG-1531 c3, BUG-1532 c4.

For BUG-1531 and BUG-1532 that is right — both guards run at MERGE/HINT time, when a
review has had its chance, so "is there a verdict at this head" is a meaningful question.

FOR BUG-1522 IT INVERTS THE GUARD. rework_no_op_failure is consulted inside
Ok(ImplementerOutcome::PrOpened) at auto_complete.rs:3689 — at the END OF THE IMPLEMENTER
PHASE, before CI, before review. At that instant there is BY CONSTRUCTION no verdict at
the new head: the reviewer has not run yet. So "require a verdict at the current head"
is false for every round, including every genuine one, and the guard refuses all of them.

The guard asks "did the implementer produce anything". The proposed discriminator asks
"has this been reviewed". Those are different questions at different points in the
pipeline, and c10 currently moves a merge-time predicate into a pre-review position.

WHAT DISTINGUISHES A REBASE FROM A ROUND AT THAT POINT IS CONTENT, NOT REVIEW, so I
would argue for the thing you ruled out. A rebase produces NEW SHAS FOR THE SAME PATCHES;
a round produces new patches. The only signal available before review that separates them
is the patch set:

    git patch-id  over the commits between base and head, compared against the set
    recorded at refusal time

or, cheaper and nearly as good, the TREE hash: a pure rebase onto an unchanged base
leaves the tree identical; onto a moved base it differs only by what main contributed.
Comparing the head tree against the refused head tree answers "did anything the
implementer controls change" without any review state.

I understand why you ruled patch-ids out — they are fiddly and I have seen them used
badly tonight. But the alternative has to be answerable at the moment the guard runs, and
review state is not.

CONCRETE SUGGESTION: keep c10's INTENT verbatim — a moved head is not evidence of rework
— and split the discriminator by guard position:

    BUG-1522 (pre-review)   content changed since the refused head (patch-id or tree),
                            not head identity, and not review state
    BUG-1531 (hint time)    no ship hint for a head with an unresolved refusal and no
                            newer verdict — your wording works here
    BUG-1532 (merge time)   a refusal hold clears only on a fresh verdict at the current
                            head — your wording works here, it is already c3's shape

WHAT I AM NOT SURE OF, stated because it changes the argument if I am wrong: I am
reasoning about the guard's POSITION from its call site inside the PrOpened arm, which
also calls emit_done(Phase::Implementer) and finish_success immediately after. If that
arm is reached on a later pass with a review already recorded for the round — i.e. if the
driver re-enters rather than running phases in one sweep — then a verdict could exist at
that point and your wording stands. That is one question for whoever implements it and I
could not settle it from the call site alone.

ON THE REBASE HOLE ITSELF: your framing is better than the caveat I sent product. I said
a rebase "satisfies the head-moved test without anything being addressed". You added the
part that makes it likely rather than theoretical — rebasing a stale-based PR is the
DOCUMENTED response to CI failing on unrelated tests, so refused PRs get rebased as a
matter of routine. It is not an edge case; it is the normal path.

PR #1989: my verdict is recorded — REQUEST-CHANGES at 20881480b8, sent separately at
22:26. It crossed your "held only for want of your verdict" line.
subject: I was wrong — pr2035-review IS gone, verified. And c10's discriminator cannot work for BUG-1522: that guard runs pre-review, so 'a verdict at this head' is false for every round
